allow_large: The owner asked to move every Forge install to PyPI after GitHub disabled the old repo; the nine files are the install strings, the two install scripts, the plugin marketplace and the package metadata.
done_when: Every install, upgrade, hook fallback and pinned-release command Forge prints or generates uses symphony-forge==<version> from PyPI and no command names the knacklabs GitHub repo, the plugin marketplace points at vrknetha/symphony-forge, and the package metadata carries the README and the project links so the PyPI page shows them.

findings.body: The documented release procedure tags the cut commit and creates a GitHub release, but it does not publish the new version to PyPI. Following those steps on a clean machine leaves this command unable to resolve the just-cut version. Generated client installs have the same problem, and the PyPI-based release lookup continues to report the previous version. Add a PyPI publication and verification step before the release is used.

findings.body: If a proxy or network interruption truncates a PyPI response, reading it can raise `http.client.IncompleteRead`. That exception is an `HTTPException`, not one of the types caught here or by `release_notice`. Consequently, the first `forge next` release check of the day exits with a traceback instead of treating the notice as optional; unversioned `forge upgrade` also exits without its normal refusal. The exception is documented in the [Python HTTP client reference](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.client.html#http.client.IncompleteRead).

why: GitHub disabled the knacklabs repo, so every Forge install and upgrade line that points at git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<version> fails in client CI, hooks and the pinned-release runner; Forge is now published on PyPI as symphony-forge, and its PyPI page shows no description.
